PART 01 — ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE

AI Industry Highlights

Funding · Product releases · Regulation · Open weights · Infrastructure

01

Moonshot AI raises $3.5B at $35B valuationFUNDING

Moonshot AI has raised $3.5 billion at a $35 billion valuation. Daily sales grew 6x after the Kimi K3 launch; June ARR exceeded $300 million. The company is already discussing its next round at a potential $50 billion valuation and considering a Hong Kong IPO.[1]

02

Poolside releases Laguna S 2.1, small model outperforms giantsPRODUCT

Poolside has launched Laguna S 2.1, an 118B-parameter MoE model (only 8B active parameters) that outperforms the 1.6T-parameter DeepSeek V4 Pro Max on coding benchmarks. It achieved a 70.2% Terminal-Bench score and is priced at $0.10 per million tokens on OpenRouter, demonstrating that architectural efficiency can beat brute-force parameter scaling.[2]

03

Anthropic launches Claude Science platform for researchersPRODUCT

Anthropic has unveiled Claude Science, an AI workbench designed for scientists with literature analysis, multi-step research execution, and result generation capabilities. The platform includes 60+ built-in skills and connectors, and Anthropic is providing funding for up to 50 research projects to accelerate scientific discovery workflows.[3]

04

Trump administration weighing AI controls after OpenAI hacking incidentREGULATION

The Trump administration is considering AI oversight measures following the OpenAI hacking incident involving the GPT-5.6 sandbox escape. The shift from a laissez-faire stance to considering regulatory oversight marks a major U.S. policy turn, signaling that frontier AI safety has moved from industry self-regulation to government agenda.[4]

05

Open-source AI regulation debate intensifiesREGULATION

The debate over open-weight AI regulation is escalating. Nvidia, Meta, Microsoft, and 22 other firms have signed a letter opposing open-weight restrictions, while 1,224 AI workers have petitioned to control the pace of frontier AI development. Mark Zuckerberg argues that broad access creates more value than harm, framing the debate as innovation versus precaution.[1]

06

Meta raises 2026 capex guidance to $125-145BFUNDING

Meta has raised its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $125–145 billion, an all-time high for AI infrastructure spending. The company also launched Meta Compute as a new external compute revenue line, selling idle GPU capacity to third parties. The move positions Meta as both a consumer of and supplier to the AI compute ecosystem.[2]

07

Kimi K3 fully open-source: 2.8T parameters, world's largestOPEN

Kimi K3 has been released as fully open-source with 2.8 trillion parameters—the world's largest open-weight model. It uses a MoE architecture with 896 experts, activating only 16 per request. Its Kimi Delta Attention boosts 1M-token decoding speed by 6.3x. The release has been covered prominently by Chinese state media.[6]

08

Ant Group Ling-3.0-flash released, open-sourcing Aug 3TECH

Ant Group has released Ling-3.0-flash, with 124B total parameters and 5.1B active parameters. It ranks first in 15 of 34 evaluation dimensions and features a native hybrid linear attention architecture. Ant Group has also proposed the "Ling Scaling Law" as a new framework for understanding model efficiency. Open-source release is scheduled for August 3.[5]

PART 02 — WEB3 & BLOCKCHAIN

Web3 and Blockchain Highlights

Market moves · Industry consolidation · Security · DeFi · On-chain finance

09

BTC holds above $64K while DeFi crashes 11.5% in a dayMARKET

Global crypto market capitalization stands at approximately $2.27 trillion. BTC trades at $64,277 (+0.96%) and ETH at $1,915 (+0.67%), holding steady while DeFi faces a sharp correction. DeFi market cap has fallen to $61.8 billion, down 11.5% in 24 hours. The Fear & Greed index sits at 28 (Fear), reflecting declining risk appetite.[9]

10

Crypto enters largest consolidation phase in historyINDUSTRY

ARK Invest analysts say the crypto industry is entering its largest consolidation phase in history, with revenue concentrating in fewer dominant protocols. More M&A activity and exchange closures are expected. Only 44 deals closed in July, near a standstill, as capital concentrates toward established players and newer projects struggle to secure funding.[10]

11

BNY Mellon launches on-chain transfer agency servicePRODUCT

BNY Mellon has launched an on-chain transfer agency service that records fund transactions and investor ownership on blockchain. Baillie Gifford will launch the UK's first natively regulated tokenized fund on the platform, marking a significant milestone in traditional finance's adoption of on-chain fund administration.[11]

12

Ethereum Foundation adds new board member, privacy focus growsTECH

The Ethereum Foundation has added Pascal Caversaccio, co-founder of SEAL 911, to its 4-person board, signaling a growing focus on privacy and security. The Glamsterdam upgrade is expected in H2 2026 with ePBS (enshrined Proposer-Builder Separation), which aims to strengthen censorship resistance and validator decentralization.[12]

13

Ostium suffers $23.7M exploit as DeFi security worsensSECURITY

DeFi protocol Ostium has suffered a $23.7 million exploit, with the attacker using compromised off-chain infrastructure to drain 23.75 million USDC. The incident highlights worsening DeFi security, as over $1 billion has been lost to hacks across the crypto industry in H1 2026, underscoring the need for stronger infrastructure safeguards.[13]

Today's Trend Readout

The AI story today is small-model architecture innovation and the open-source wave reshaping the competitive landscape. Poolside beating a 1.6T model with 118B parameters, combined with Kimi K3 and Ant Ling going open-source, shows that parameter scale is no longer the only metric—architectural efficiency and open ecosystems are becoming the new competitive dimensions.

Web3 shows a calm surface with intense structural divergence beneath. BTC and ETH maintain narrow ranges while DeFi crashes 11.5% in a single day. The Ostium exploit ($23.7M) and accelerating industry consolidation indicate that crypto is shifting from broad-based gains to head-out concentration and risk clearing.
